name: Annotation appearance-synthesis policy
description: What excise draws for an annotation that ships no /AP /N, as DATA: one row per (subtype, state, condition), each carrying the decision, the measured oracle evidence as bbox + shape rather than a bare count, the majority verdict with the size of the pool it was taken over, and the fixture the measurement came from. Re-measured by Excise.Rendering.Tests/Differential/AnnotationSynthesisPolicyGateTests.cs; the renderer it pins is Excise.Rendering/SkiaRenderer.Annotations.cs.
whyThisExists: The policy used to live in scattered ifs justified by free-text comments nothing re-measured, and three separate errors came out of the same mechanism - a decision made from a scalar that cannot represent the thing being decided. #885 drew a blue box on every widget, justified by 'mutool 233 px, pdftocairo 229, excise 0': those pixels were the CHECK MARK, and neither oracle drew any box. #987's /Link border default was decided on a fixture that did state /BS /W 2, so the no-/Border-at-all case - the common one - was never measured. #972's own first fix drew a CARET instead of a tick with identical pixel count and identical bbox. An ink count cannot tell a tick from a box, and a bbox cannot tell a tick from a caret.
rules: MAJORITY, NEVER A SINGLE ORACLE. A row draws only when more than half the voting engines draw. #972's radio case is 1-of-3 and stays unimplemented for exactly that reason (the #875 trap).

WHERE NO MAJORITY DRAWS, EXCISE DRAWS NOTHING. A row whose decision contradicts its own majority verdict must carry a 'deviation' block naming a kind, an issue and a reason. There are TWO such rows and they are the interesting ones - there were four until the pool grew from 3 engines to 5 (#1007/#1009) and line.without-color's majority reversed under it, and three until #1005 stopped widget.sig.unsigned inventing a signature placeholder no majority draws.

EVIDENCE IS BBOX + SHAPE, NEVER A BARE COUNT. Each evidence entry records the inked-pixel count for scale, the bbox, and the bbox's relationship to the annotation rect. The gate asserts the vote and the bbox class; it holds the count only to a factor of two, because tool versions drift.

SHAPE ASSERTIONS WHERE COUNT AND BBOX CANNOT DISCRIMINATE. widget.tx.value-negative-size-centered is the proof: mutool's mirrored value has the same pixel count and the same bbox as the upright one, and only the ink profiles tell them apart.

A DIFFERENCE THAT ORIGINATES IN SKIA'S RASTERISATION IS AN ACCEPTED LIMITATION, not a defect and not something to compensate for. Do not tune a shape predicate or special-case a fixture to force agreement. Before re-triaging one, read tests/skia-rasterisation-register.json (#1011): the ones already traced to Skia are recorded there with their evidence, and so is one claim that was re-measured and did NOT hold - the 1 pt link border that supposedly inked 800 px against poppler's 400 inks 400, exactly as poppler does.

VOTES ARE COUNTED PER ENGINE, NOT PER BINARY. pdftocairo and pdftoppm are two rasterisers over ONE annotation-synthesis implementation (poppler); counting both would give poppler two votes out of four. pdftoppm is measured anyway, as a cross-check on the poppler vote, with counts:false.

AN ENGINE VOTES ON A ROW ONLY WHERE IT COULD HAVE DRAWN ONE - so `counts` is per EVIDENCE ENTRY, not per oracle. Ghostscript's zero on a non-printable fixture is the original example (hence everyFixtureIsPrintable); pdfbox and pdfium on the Widget rows are two more, and both were measured rather than assumed: pdfium renders no widget at all through FPDF_RenderPageBitmap, even one that ships an /AP, and pdfbox generates field appearances only in PDAcroForm.refreshAppearances(), which rendering never calls. Counting either zero would have flipped Widget rows toward 'blank' on the strength of two engines that were never asked the question. Every abstaining entry is still MEASURED and recorded, with an 'abstention' key naming which kind it is, so the arithmetic can be redone by anyone who disagrees with the call.

A SHAPE PREDICATE CANNOT SEE A MAGNITUDE, so a row may additionally pin its GEOMETRY with 'exciseInkMatchesDrawers': excise's ink bbox must land inside the spread of the bboxes the DRAWING voters recorded, edge by edge, within a stated tolerance. #1003 and #1004 are why it exists - both were rows where every other check in this gate was green while excise drew the right picture at visibly the wrong size (a highlight 6 px too wide at each end; a fitted field value 64 px wide where every engine draws 90-94). It is opt-in per row and per AXIS, because the axes diverge independently: widget.tx.value-auto-size pins x while its vertical placement is tracked separately as #1016.
everyFixtureIsPrintable: Every fixture carries /F 4 (Print), and that is load-bearing rather than tidy. Ghostscript renders ONLY printable annotations, so on a fixture without /F it reports zero inked pixels for reasons that have nothing to do with the annotation - a structural ABSTENTION that reads exactly like a 'draws nothing' vote. That misreading is already in the record this table replaces: #987's link border looked 1-of-3 on pdfium bug_821454.pdf (whose links carry no /F) and was 2-of-3 once the fixture was printable (3-of-5 now that pdfbox and pdfium vote); #972's checkbox table recorded Ghostscript as drawing nothing 'in any of these' cases; #885's Stamp row read 2-of-3 and became 3-of-3 on a printable fixture (3-of-5 now). The parenthesised numbers are the CURRENT pool - see oraclePool; the ones before them are what the same rows read under the three-engine pool, kept because the point of the entry is the misreading, not the count.

pdftoppm.reason: same poppler annotation-synthesis code as pdftocairo; a second rasteriser is not a second opinion. Measured as a cross-check.

pdfbox.reason: PDFBox 3.0.3 (tools/vendor/pdfbox-app-3.0.3.jar) under Homebrew openjdk 26.0.1 at /opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk/bin/java. It synthesizes markup appearances IN the rendering path (its handlers package: Square, Circle, Line, Polygon, PolyLine, Ink, Highlight, Underline, StrikeOut, Squiggly, FreeText, Link, Text, FileAttachment), so on those rows it is a full voter. It abstains on the Widget rows: measured, PDFBox renders a widget that ships an /AP /N (6400 px on a probe fixture), so its rendering path is engaged and only the SYNTHESIS is absent - field appearances come from PDAcroForm.refreshAppearances(), which rendering never calls. Calling it explicitly on this table's own Widget fixtures produces the text-field values (264-770 px, the same order as the three voting engines' 250-753) and still nothing for /Btn, /Ch and /Sig. So a render-time zero on a Widget row says when PDFBox generates field appearances, not what it thinks one looks like.
pdfbox.previousReasonWasFalse: Until #1009 this said 'abstains: needs a JRE, which the measurement host does not have'. The host has had one throughout: /usr/bin/java is a macOS stub that reports 'Unable to locate a Java Runtime' even with a JDK installed, and that stub is what the earlier measurement asked. PdfBoxReferenceRenderer.ResolveJavaCommand() probes the Homebrew path first, so nothing had to be installed and no env var had to be set - a whole engine was excluded from 44 rows by a misread error message.

pdfium.reason: Rendered through PdfiumNativeReferenceRenderer with renderAnnotations: true, i.e. FPDF_RenderPageBitmap with FPDF_ANNOT (#1007). pdfium synthesizes an /AP for the fixed subtype list its core AP generator covers - measured here as Text, FreeText, Square, Circle, Ink, Highlight, Underline, StrikeOut, Squiggly - and nothing for Link, Line, Polygon, PolyLine, Stamp, FileAttachment, Sound and Redact, which is a real blank vote from an engaged generator. It abstains on the Widget rows: measured, pdfium draws nothing for a widget even when the /AP /N IS present, so FPDF_RenderPageBitmap does not render widgets at all - they belong to the form-fill layer (FPDFDOC_InitFormFillEnvironment / FPDF_FFLDraw), which this harness does not drive.
pdfium.flagsZeroWasTheOldBlocker: Until #1007 this oracle called FPDF_RenderPageBitmap with flags=0 and therefore inked ZERO on all 44 rows. The fix is opt-in and defaults to the old behaviour, so no corpus baseline moves; only callers asking about annotations pass true. Mutation-checked: with renderAnnotations:false the same sweep measures 0 inked px on all 44 fixtures, with true it inks on 13.

oraclePool.measured: 2026-08-16, macOS, mutool 1.26 / poppler / Ghostscript on PATH, PDFBox 3.0.3 on openjdk 26.0.1, pdfium via tools/vendor/pdfium with FPDF_ANNOT
oraclePool.size: 5 voting engines on the 27 non-Widget rows (mupdf, poppler, ghostscript, pdfbox, pdfium); 3 on the 17 Widget rows (pdfbox and pdfium abstain there, see rules)
oraclePool.beforeThisPass: 3 voting engines on all 44 rows. pdfium inked zero everywhere because the oracle passed flags=0 (#1007); pdfbox was excluded by a reason that was false when written (#1009).
oraclePool.agreement: A MEASUREMENT WITH A DATE, not a property - recompute it, do not quote it. Unanimity across the voting engines fell from 29/44 (65.9%) to 25/44 (56.8%) purely by adding voters; on the 27 non-Widget rows it is 14/27. Pairwise: ghostscript-poppler 39/44 (88.6%), ghostscript-pdfbox 24/27 (88.9%), pdfbox-poppler 23/27 (85.2%), mupdf-pdfbox 20/27 (74.1%), mupdf-poppler 32/44 (72.7%), ghostscript-mupdf 31/44 (70.5%), mupdf-pdfium 19/27 (70.4%), pdfbox-pdfium and pdfium-poppler 18/27 (66.7%), ghostscript-pdfium 17/27 (63.0%). The lone-dissenter count changed shape: over 3 engines mupdf dissented alone on 10 of 15 split rows; over the larger pool there are 19 split rows and the lone dissenter is mupdf 4, ghostscript 3, pdfium 3, poppler 1 - mupdf's apparent eccentricity was partly an artefact of a three-engine pool in which poppler and Ghostscript agree 88.6% of the time.
oraclePool.onlyOneVerdictMoved: line.without-color, from 2-of-3 draw to 2-of-5 blank. No row acquired a new deviation. Widget verdicts are untouched by construction.

shapeVocabulary.none: no ink anywhere on the page
shapeVocabulary.hollow-rect-on-annot-rect: ink bbox matches the annotation rect; the interior is empty
shapeVocabulary.filled-rect-on-annot-rect: ink bbox matches the annotation rect; the interior is inked
shapeVocabulary.hollow-oval-on-annot-rect: as hollow-rect, and the corners of the rect are empty
shapeVocabulary.inset-tick: a mark strictly inside the rect on all four sides whose lowest row centroid is left of centre - a tick, not a caret and not a border
shapeVocabulary.marker-at-anchor: a filled marker of roughly fixed size anchored at the rect's top-left corner (§12.5.6.4 /Text)
shapeVocabulary.text-value-inside-rect: a wide, short run of ink entirely inside the rect
shapeVocabulary.mirrored-text-value: text-value-inside-rect whose column profile is the REVERSE of the row named by comparedWith, and correlates better reversed than unreversed
shapeVocabulary.clipped-remnant-inside-rect: some ink, all of it inside the rect, and far less than the row named by comparedWith draws - what survives clipping when the run lands outside
shapeVocabulary.stroked-path-inside-rect: ink inside the rect that fills little of its own bbox - a stroke, not a fill
shapeVocabulary.horizontal-band: a line spanning the quad's width, a small fraction of its height

howToUpdate: By hand, from the gate's failure message, which prints what it measured. There is deliberately no --update flag: this file records decisions and the evidence they rest on, and a regenerator would let a behaviour change rewrite its own justification. That is the failure mode scripts/update-corpus-expectations.sh has already caused twice.

rows.condition: /BS or /Border states a width greater than zero
neither /Border nor /BS is present - the §12.5.6.5 default /Border [0 0 1] applies
/BS present with no /W - Table 168 makes the default width 1
/Border [0 0 0] - the standard way to say 'no visible border'
/Border present but with fewer than the three required entries
a stated width wider than half the annotation's smaller side

deviation.note: THREE engines draw now and they agree on nothing: pdftocairo covers the whole page (40000 px, bbox (0,0)-(200,200)), Ghostscript clamps to a frame of its own choosing (11926 px, bbox (38,38)-(163,163)), PDFBox fills the annotation rect exactly (10000 px on a 100x100 rect). mutool and pdfium draw nothing. Copying any of them is electing a renderer, and all three bury the page content the border is supposed to outline. excise refuses and says so in a diagnostic. The enlarged pool (#1007/#1009) took this from 2-of-3 to 3-of-5 and made the disagreement about GEOMETRY worse, not better, which is the deviation's whole argument. ACCEPTED, not pending: see #1015 (decision record). Previously cited #885, a closed work item that does not record this reasoning. There is no work to do here — nothing anyone implements makes three disagreeing engines agree. The falsifying condition is the drawers CONVERGING, which the gate re-measures every run.

/FT /Btn with field flag bit 16 (radio) and /AS on

3 of 3. The #972 note that 'mutool honours /MK here; Poppler ignores it' does not survive re-measurement on a printable widget: poppler inks the same 2500 px over the same rect. (Widget rows have a THREE-engine pool: pdfbox and pdfium abstain structurally, see rules.)

rows.condition: /MK states a background and NO border colour
rows.note: Added by #1005, which removed the OTHER user of the same invented colour. A /MK that sets /BG and no /BC used to get the identical neutral-blue 1 pt stroke the signature placeholder got. Measured here: mutool, pdftocairo, pdftoppm and Ghostscript each ink exactly the 50x50 fill and no border at all, so the border is now drawn only where /MK /BC states one. The three voting engines agree to the pixel, which is why this row also carries the geometry pin.

exciseInkMatchesDrawers.note: The fill IS the picture here, so both axes are pinned and the tolerance is ZERO: excise inks exactly the drawers' 50x50 bbox, pixel for pixel, and the geometry is integral with antialiasing off in this gate, so nothing legitimate moves it. Zero is also what makes the pin sensitive to the defect it records - the invented 1 pt border straddles the /Rect edge and grows the ink bbox by exactly 1 px on the right and bottom, which any looser tolerance would wave through.

rows.condition: /FT /Tx with /V and a /DA stating a positive Tf size
the same value with /Q 1 (centred) - the reference the mirrored row below is compared against
/DA states a NEGATIVE Tf size (a real size that mirrors, not auto-size), /Q 1
rows.note: The row that a count and a bbox cannot decide: mutool's and pdftocairo's mirrored value occupies EXACTLY the upright value's bbox with the same pixel count. Only the profiles tell them apart - the column profile is the reverse of the upright one and the row profile is its flip.

rows.condition: negative Tf size, /Q 0 (left) - the mirrored run advances LEFT out of the field
negative Tf size, /Q 2 (right) - the signed width pushes the run past the field

rows.note: The clip is the load-bearing part: mutool and pdftocairo stop at the /Rect, Ghostscript does not, and excise used to run off the PAGE.

rows.condition: /DA states Tf size 0 - auto-size, fit the text to the field

exciseInkMatchesDrawers.note: #1003. /DA states Tf size 0, so the value is fitted to the field (12.7.4.3). RenderTextFieldValue used min(rect.Height * 0.75, 16) - height-only, capped, blind to the value and to the field width alike - and drew the value 64 px wide where all three voters draw it 90-94. AutoFitFontSize now takes the smaller of two limits read off the resolved typeface: the string's own advance must fit the width, and the font's own line box (ascent + descent) must fit the height. Ink bbox of /V (Mountain) at 72 dpi in a 100x30 field - mutool 94x18, pdftocairo 92x18, ghostscript 90x18, old excise 64x12, now 92x17. The rule is settled by a 100x100 field, where mutool (94x18) and poppler (92x18) draw the value at exactly the size they use in the 30 pt-tall one: the fit is bounded by WIDTH, and no absolute cap is involved. Ghostscript is the outlier there (136x57), the same disagreement it shows on widget.tx.value-wider-than-the-rect. The vertical rule was a flat cap-height approximation (fontSize * 0.7) that is no real font's, drawing the value 2-5 px high with the error scaling by size; it now centres the font's OWN line box (ascent + descent) read from the resolved typeface - the same metrics AutoFitFontSize uses to pick the size. Ink bbox went [54,112,146,129] -> [54,115,146,132] against mutool [53,115,147,133], pdftocairo [53,117,145,135], ghostscript [53,116,143,134]: the TOP edge now lands inside the drawers' spread exactly. The x extent is deliberately not a cross-platform pixel pin: an unembedded Helvetica resolves through CoreText on macOS and FreeType on Linux, and the latter measured a narrower fit while remaining correctly inside the field. Shape and width-fit behaviour remain asserted; the portable y-placement regression stays pinned to 2 px.

rows.condition: /V present and no /DA on the widget or the AcroForm

rows.history: Until #1005 this row read decision 'draw', shape 'hollow-rect-on-annot-rect', and carried a deviation of kind 'invented-ink': RenderWidgetDefault treated /FT /Sig as explicitly styled and stroked a neutral blue 1 pt rectangle over the whole /Rect - 520 inked px, bbox (49,109)-(151,141). #885 added it so an unsigned signature field would read as 'sign here'. The evidence never supported it: of the three engines that vote on a Widget row, poppler and Ghostscript draw nothing and mutool draws a 23x5 mark in the field's top-left corner, which is not a border - so excise both elected an outlier (the #875 trap) and drew something the outlier does not draw. Now removed, and this row agrees with its own majority verdict. A /FT /Sig that carries /MK still gets that styling by the /MK rule; making an unsigned field visible in the editor is an overlay the GUI can draw, not ink in the rendered page.

rows.condition: /Text with no /AP, including the degenerate /Rect §12.5.6.4 makes normal

rows.condition: /Square or /Circle with no /C - no colour is stated, so there is nothing to draw with
rows.note: 2 of 5 (poppler and pdfium stroke it black; mutool, Ghostscript and PDFBox draw nothing). The enlarged pool moved this from 1-of-3 to 2-of-5 without moving the verdict - still no majority, so excise still draws nothing.

THE ONE ROW THE ENLARGED POOL REVERSES (#1007/#1009). It read 2-of-3 draw - pdftocairo 242 px, Ghostscript 242 px, mutool 0 - and therefore carried a deviation of kind 'known-defect-not-yet-fixed' filed as #1006, on the reading that excise's blank contradicted the majority. With PDFBox and pdfium voting it is 2-of-5: PDFBox draws a /Line that HAS /C (326 px on line.with-color) and draws nothing here, and pdfium draws neither (no /Line in its AP generator's subtype list), so three of five engines leave a /Line with no /C blank and excise is now WITH the majority, not against it. The deviation block is removed because the gate forbids one on a row that agrees with its verdict; #1006 is kept here because the change is in the EVIDENCE, not in the renderer - nothing about excise moved, and whoever closes or re-scopes #1006 should read this row first. The old deviation's supporting argument is preserved: CreateAnnotationStrokePaint returns null when /C is absent, documented as 'viewers differ here and none of the corpus fixtures omit /C', and viewers do indeed differ - 2 to 3.

exciseInkMatchesDrawers.note: #1004. The ends of a highlight overshoot the /QuadPoints in every engine that draws one, and by how much is measured rather than chosen: the overshoot scales with the quad's HEIGHT and ignores its width. Px past each end at 72 dpi on a 100 pt quad, at quad heights 8/10/20/40 - mutool 2/2/4/8, pdftocairo 2/2/4/8, pdftoppm 2/2/4/8, ghostscript 1/2/3/5, pdfbox 2/2/5/8, pdfium 0/0/0/0, height/5 = 1.6/2/4/8. RenderTextMarkupDefault used min(height,width)/2, which drew 10 px past each end of this row's 20 px quad - 6 px wider than every oracle on both sides - and on a narrow quad shrank with the WIDTH, which no engine does (a 10x40 quad still overshoots 8 in mutool, poppler and pdfbox). It is now height/5, which is what mutool, poppler and pdfbox draw and which sits inside the spread of everything that draws anything: excise's bbox went from (40,80)-(160,100) to (46,80)-(154,100), against mutool and pdftocairo's (46,80)-(154,100). Pinned on x because that is the axis the inflation moves; the band's top and bottom are the quad's own.

deviation.note: 3 of 5 draw and the three disagree by 4.7x on how much and by a factor of 3.6 on the bbox height (mutool 1055 px in a band, pdftocairo 4946 px over the whole rect, Ghostscript 1564 px in a band); PDFBox and pdfium draw nothing at all - neither has a /Stamp appearance handler. A stamp's picture is viewer-specific art; there is nothing to copy, only an invitation to invent some. The enlarged pool (#1007/#1009) took this from a unanimous 3-of-3 to a bare 3-of-5, so the majority that this row already declines to follow is now the thinnest one in the table. The older 2-of-3 reading was measured on a non-printable fixture, so Ghostscript's zero was an abstention. ACCEPTED, not pending: see #1015 (decision record). Previously cited #889, a closed work item that does not record this reasoning. There is no work to do here — nothing anyone implements makes three disagreeing engines agree. The falsifying condition is the drawers CONVERGING, which the gate re-measures every run.
